label: app:<group>
asserts: the build MANIFEST: this diff touches apps/<group>/, or touches shared/ which every app pins. Derived from the diff and recomputed on every push; a hand edit does not survive

label: itil:standard
asserts: the ITIL change TYPE: the diff is limited to pre-authorised paths. Says what kind of change this is, never how far it has got

label: itil:normal
asserts: the ITIL change TYPE: the diff touches router/, gates/, change/, targets/ or .github/, so it needs a human approval

label: itil:emergency
asserts: THIS change is the remedy. Passes the freeze and the queue; exempts nothing else. Never derived, because only a person may declare an emergency

label: control-plane
asserts: this change alters how every FUTURE change is verified, so the pipeline cannot verify it. Narrower than itil:normal and a soak trigger

label: labeler:skip
asserts: a person is taking the manifest back: app:* becomes asserted rather than derived. A declared deviation in label form

label: change:requested
asserts: a person has raised a change request. The only label a person adds to set a change going, and the whole of their part

label: release
asserts: take this one all the way NOW rather than waiting for a slot. Names no environment because it asks for the whole path. The scheduler consumes it; a trigger that stays on re-fires

label: change:scheduled
asserts: a window has been booked for this change on the change schedule. A record; nothing blocks on it

label: release:start
asserts: the release has BEGUN for the booked change request, and names which change is in flight. A person cannot truthfully assert this

label: deploy:staging
asserts: ACTION IN FLIGHT plus the BERTH CLAIM guard 1 reads. Not a request to deploy: adding it by hand asserts that the guards were re-checked when nobody checked anything

label: deploy:production
asserts: ACTION IN FLIGHT: the workflow is deploying to production right now

label: staging:in-progress
asserts: the staging deploy is running. Cleared when the run ends, either way

label: blocked:queue
asserts: another open PR holds the berth. Set and cleared by the queue; a fact about the estate rendered onto this change

label: blocked:lock
asserts: the deployment lock is held by another change and is not yet stale

label: blocked:freeze
asserts: a freeze or an in-flight emergency covers the requested window

label: blocked:diverged
asserts: main moved under a change production is already serving. PRODUCTION IS AHEAD OF MAIN, and not recoverable by merging. A human may clear it after rebasing

label: change:complete
asserts: TERMINAL for VALIDATION: every guard passed and production was observed serving this build. Set before the merge, because the merge follows completion rather than constituting it

label: change:failed
asserts: ITIL closure code. The change did not complete: production never served it, or never had it made live. Nothing to undo

label: change:backed-out
asserts: ITIL closure code. Production DID serve this change and was returned to a named prior state. Refused without --to <sha>, because the word asserts an estate action

label: change:backfill-owed
asserts: AN UNPAID CHANGE RECORD: this change reached main without the normal evidence and still owes the window, the observations and the reason. Blocks nothing. Persistent, because the merge is when the debt STARTS

label: staging:e2e
asserts: the contracts held on staging, measured by the e2e gate against the staging slot. The AUTHORIZING run is this one, never the in-runner one

label: staging:e2e-failed
asserts: the e2e gate measured a failure on staging. A recorded failure outranks a pass beside it

label: staging:smoke
asserts: a browser could actually use staging

label: staging:smoke-failed
asserts: the smoke gate measured a failure on staging

label: staging:uat
asserts: THE EXCEPTION: for acceptance the person IS the instrument. Recorded via change/observe.sh, which refuses unless the URL is serving this PR's head. Not repeatable, so the label is durable and a person may withdraw it

label: production:e2e
asserts: the contracts held in production

label: production:e2e-failed
asserts: the e2e gate measured a failure in production

label: production:smoke
asserts: a browser could use production

label: production:smoke-failed
asserts: the smoke gate measured a failure in production

label: production:healthy
asserts: CONVERGENCE: N samples through the front all reported this build. Sampled, never attested; it cannot enumerate replicas. Typed by hand once on #9, which was the ownership defect

label: freeze
asserts: ESTATE STATE, on issue #1 and never on a PR: ordinary change is suspended for everyone, including whoever declared it. Only ever READ in-tree, which is why the label auditor cannot see it

label: emergency
asserts: ESTATE STATE, on issue #1 and never on a PR: an emergency is in flight somewhere, everything stops, and it grants NO exemption to whatever carries it. Kept separate from itil:emergency so the write that closes the estate cannot exempt its own carrier

label: hold:staging
asserts: REJECTED SEMANTICS. A per-change human stop. Its job is covered by freeze (the estate stops) and by the earlier human stops: not requesting, and not approving

label: staging:passed
asserts: RETIRED: named no measurement and no environment, so it could be satisfied by observing something else. Replaced by the staging:* stack

label: staging:failed
asserts: RETIRED: same defect as staging:passed

label: deployed:production
asserts: RETIRED: replaced by change:complete plus the deployment record

label: deployed:staging-<group>-<n>
asserts: SPECIFIED, NOT BUILT: a staging slot deployed this group at this build. spec.org requires it on the head SHA before production; nothing in the tree writes it
